original.description: COPERNICUS SPACE COMPONENT - COMPETITIVE FRAME CONTRACTS -ESA Ground Segment Operations Framework Production Service This procurement targets the delivery of the Copernicus Sentinels Production Operations Service (Copernicus Production Service). The CopernicusProduction Service is a key element of the Copernicus Space Component (CSC) operations in charge of generating the Copernicus user level data for each Sentinel satellite, starting from the acquired satellite data stream. The Copernicus Production Service includesthe following functionalities:-Systematic production for processing all the satellite data acquired into a set of pre-defined user level data that are made systematically and fully available to users;-On-demand production, allowing the generation of any user level data from archived lower level user data -Reprocessing, for the bulk re-generation of user level data Copernicus Production Service will be based on service providers' technical solution in line with the ESA defined interfaces, and the use of the Instrument Data Processors (IPF) provided by ESA for the generation of the user level data.The performance of the Copernicus Production Service will be managed through a Service Level Agreement and the measurement of the service performance itself through a set of Key Performance Indicators.The Copernicus Production Service will be procured through the ESA Framework Agreements procedure, as established at Article 15 of ESA Procurement Regulations (ESA/REG/001, rev. 3 which can be downloaded at the following URL: http://emits.sso.esa.int/emits/owa/emits.main). This procedure follows a two-steps procurement approach:-Step 1 - Qualification Phase: Qualification process established through an Open Competition (Frame Invitation To Tender - Frame ITT) resulting in the award of Frame Contracts between the Agency and several service providers. Step 1 bidding period will be open until December 2021 at the earliest. -Step 2 - Implementation Phase: Restricted Competitions (Request for Proposal - RFP) between the Frame Contractors qualified under Step1resulting into the award of Work Order(s) between the Agency and one or more Frame Contractors for the implementation of the  Copernicus Production Service.The Copernicus Production Service procurement is funded by the Copernicus Programme and will be open exclusively to economic operators which have their registered office in an EU Member State or a State participating in the Copernicus Programme.The Frame ITT package (Cover Letter, Frame Statement of Work, Special Conditions of Tender, Draft Frame Contract) will be available on ESA tendering website (EMITS http://emits.sso.esa.int/emits/owa/emits.main). In order to access the ITT Package from EMITS, Tenderers must be registered in esa-star as a potential ESA supplier. Any Tenderer which is not yet registered with ESA as a potential supplier must complete the online questionnaire on esa-star, under the tab "Entity registration". Further information onthe registration process can be found in ESA's INDUSTRY PORTAL available at:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/esa-star_open_for_businessPlease note that esa-star allows two levels of entity registration: "Light" and "Valid Full". This allows new users wishing to do business with ESA to carry out their registration in two steps. A "Light" registration will grant access to all esa-star services up to and including proposal submission. The award of ESA contracts requires  registration.to have status "Valid Full"

original.description: The European Space Agency ("the Agency" or "ESA") invites you to submit a Proposal under the General Support Technology Programme, Element 1: "Preparation of enabling space technologies and building blocks''The aim is to prepare and to develop enabling capabilities and the associated building blocks for space related systems and the associated sub-systems. An additional aim is to allow the targeted and coordinated development of the capabilities and building blocks (i.e. among academia and industry) in a given ESA Member State or across different Member States (in a collaborative manner). The intended output is to provide industry with a stronger foundation (i.e. building on this acquired know-how) in order to contribute to new space related system opportunities at national or international levels (institutional, commercial...) The objective is to enable Member States to support the further development of t capabilities and the associated building blocks in their industry. The technology development activities may be prepared in a targeted and coordinated manner. The enabling capabilities and building blocks are to be developed for a targeted type and class of space systems (in terms of performance, cost, size...) and with guiding specifications. The developments are to be performed in a coordinated manner to ensure that industry is able to work on complementary capabilities. The developments may be performed within one Member State or across several Member States in a collaborative manner. The enabling capabilities and building blocks are to be developed to a level such that the industrial entities may then be able to perform developments and eventually produce for concrete/more specific space related developments. The developments may go from a proof-of-concept (via simulation or experiment) up to an engineering qualification model (EQM). They address any technical area (structures, avionics/GNC, power control and distribution...). The spefications are to be linked to the guiding system or sub-system specifications. The maximum amount per activity is 1,000 K. The maximum duration is24 months.

original.description: The ACCESS (Accelerating Commercialisation and Competitiveness of the European Space Sector) programme helps companies develop innovative commercial products and services that strengthen European competitiveness in both space and non-space markets. It fosters a diverse and dynamic space ecosystem, ensuring that the benefits of commercialisation reach all Participating States.Business Applications and Space Solutions (BASS) is the element of ACCESS programme specifically designed to accelerate the transformation of innovative ideas into market-ready space-based services and applications that deliver measurable socio-economic impact.BASS offers to companies and academia derisking tools to mitigate technical and commercial risks, shortening the path from concept to market. With a strong user-driven focus, BASS creates the conditions for commercial success and positions space as a driver of innovation, competitiveness, and lasting value for society.To deliver these outcomes, BASS offers a comprehensive support package which includes zero-equity funding, tailored business and technical expertise, project management guidance, ESA branding, and access to commercialisation networks. This ecosystem connects companies with customers, investors, and partners, enabling them to overcome market barriers whilesecuring sustainable growth through private investment and demand-driven adoption.BASS support is tailored to every stage of developmentfrom assessing the viability of new space-based applications, to designing, implementing, and piloting space-based solutions and supporting their expansion into new markets.

original.description: The overall goal of ARTES 4.0 Business Applications can be summarised as the development of pre-operational services - possibly in partnership - for a wide range of users through the combination of different systems. Business Applications activities aim at: i) collecting user feedback for better tuning of the applications and the operation of all elements involved, ii) developing commercial sustainable space based applications by linking user needs to corresponding solutions incorporating space assets requesting only limited technology adaptations, iii) demonstrating to users and stakeholders that the proposed solutions work in their operational environment and are compatible with their operational practices, iv) utilising at least one space asset (such as Satellite Communications, Earth Observation, Satellite Navigation, Human Spaceflight, or any other space asset, service or technology), leading to a better exploitation of existing space capacity and know-how together with a better understanding of how they should evolve to respond to user needs. ARTES 4.0 Business Applications operates via a 'Call for Proposals' which is always open. Partners respond with proposals as they find it opportune. The activities proposed in response to this 'Call for Proposals' must be relevant to above mentioned ARTES 4.0 Business Applications objectives. Although not a competitive tender action, this Call for Proposals' is published on esa-star Publication in order to achieve a higher degree of visibility. original.description: The InCubed Element of the European Earth Watch Programme (InCubed) aims to accompany European economic operators in the rapid evolution of the Earth Observation market, both in Europe and globally. InCubed introduces a dedicated process within ESA Earth Observation programmes to strengthen and stimulate the development of near-to-market commercial initiatives in partnership with industry. Activities supported under InCubed include the development and/or demonstration of space assets (e.g. missions, instruments, prototype elements of EO constellations), innovative mission management solutions (including for future EO constellations), as well as the development of ground, data, and application platforms. InCubed targets commercial viability by the end of the activity (at least at minimum viable product level) and requires a substantial degree of innovation, i.e. the creation of new value within the EO commercial landscape. Commercial customer engagement is mandatory, with customers acting as beta testers and validators of the developed product or service. Customer engagement must be clearly demonstrated at both pitch and proposal stages, and letters of support or interest from potential customers are considered a strong asset. The scope of the proposed activities is defined by the economic operators themselves, in line with the objectives of InCubed. Two development cycles are available within InCubed, depending on the maturity of the concept: De-risking Cycle (typically starting from TRL 4), focusing on reducing technical and market risks;Product Development Cycle (typically starting from TRL 6), aiming at delivering a product ready for commercialisation. Under this Call for Proposals, economic operators are invited to submit their ideas via the OSIP (Open Space Innovation Platform) (ideas.esa.int), which serves as the entry point for the programme. The application process consists of the following step: Idea Pitch - Applicantssubmit and present a draft Outline proposal via OSIP to ESA (and potentially the relevant National Delegation(s)). Following a positive assessment, economic operators will be invited to submit a Proposal Part 2 (Full) in accordance with the established procedures and evaluation criteria. Activities supported under InCubed are based on a co-funding scheme, whereby economic operators contribute financially to the project, demonstrating commitment to and confidence in their business case.
